chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ja'far ibn Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Hamadani, and he was with us as a pilgrim, he said:

I wrote to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) via my father, 'May I be your ransom, our companions have differed regarding the Sa' (measure). Some say the Fitrah (alms of fasting) is paid with the Meccan Sa', and some say with the Iraqi Sa'. He wrote to me: 'The Sa is six Artals in the Meccan measure and nine Artals in the Iraqi measure.' He informed me that by weight it is one thousand and seventy mithqals.

key_terms.الصَّاع: Sa, a traditional unit of volume for measuring dry goods
key_terms.الْفِطْرَةُ: Fitrah, specifically Zakat al-Fitr (alms of fasting)
key_terms.صَاعِ الْعِرَاقِيِّ: The Iraqi Sa, a different standard of volume
key_terms.صَاعِ الْمَدَنِيِّ: The Meccan Sa, a specific standard of volume
key_terms.وَزْنَةً: Mithqal, a unit of gold weight

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the Meccan and Iraqi Sa for Zakat al-Fitr?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Rida (AS) resolves the scholarly disagreement regarding the volume of the 'Sa' used for Zakat al-Fitr by providing precise metrological conversions: the Meccan Sa is defined as six Artals, while the Iraqi Sa is nine Artals. It further specifies the weight equivalent as 1,170 'Wazn', reflecting the practical need for standardized measurement in communal religious obligations during the early Shia scholarly period.
